detailed_description: The JSON to Python converter generates Python class-style code from one pasted top-level JSON object. You can set the class name, choose @dataclass, Pydantic BaseModel, TypedDict, or plain class output, toggle Optional typing, load a sample JSON object, convert, review errors for invalid input, and copy the generated code. The component uses JSON.parse and local helper functions to infer fields and nested classes from representative values. It does not accept arrays as the top-level input, import JSON files, generate code from JSON Schema, provide side-by-side structure comparison, configure naming conventions or field validation rules, emit Literal types, guarantee strict type safety, or add Pydantic validators from schema constraints.
usage_steps: Paste a top-level JSON object or load the sample.
Set the class name for the generated Python code.
Choose the output style: dataclass, Pydantic BaseModel, TypedDict, or plain class.
Toggle Optional typing if you want optional-style annotations where supported by the helper.
Click Convert, review any error message, and copy the generated Python output.
usage_examples: Generate a starter dataclass from a small JSON API response sample.
Create a basic Pydantic BaseModel draft from representative object data.
Try TypedDict output for a flat or nested JSON object before manual cleanup.
Use the sample loader to see the expected top-level object format.
